about: Written by hand: how each program assembles the server from the shared crates, as an ordered flow. Each step names the public items it uses as crate::path; generate.py stops if one is no longer there. Which implementation fills which slot is also derived from the code and shown beside this.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Flags, the config file and defaults become the server's settings and limits; the key files are checked, which gives the admission of /mcp, the web page and /mcp-admin.

steps.title: Database
steps.text: A SqlitePlace for the database file, adopting a database from before kkt-db, opens it with the core's tables; the kkt-db Database it gives is the store's database.

steps.title: Run record
steps.text: What produced this run is stored, and new rows carry its ID.

steps.title: Parts
steps.text: The store, the system clock, the operating system's randomness and key mode's identity go into the server's parts.

steps.title: Config
steps.text: The three admissions from the key check, the allowed hosts and the limits go into the server's config: admin_admission is the admin key, as AdminAdmission::SharedKey.

steps.title: Build and run
steps.text: build assembles the server from the parts and config; listen binds it; serve_until answers until a stop signal, and the program logs a socket option it could not set.

also.title: kkt watch
also.text: The command picks a client for the server, Remote (as an agent) or AdminRemote (with --admin), and hands it to kkt-watch's run with the system clock.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: The same config file as kkt serve, read through kkt-settings, and the same key check.

steps.title: Database
steps.text: A SqlitePlace opens the database file with the core's tables. It adopts no database from before kkt-db.

steps.title: Run record
steps.text: The run is recorded as kkt serve's is.

steps.title: Parts and config
steps.text: The same parts as kkt serve, with KeyMode; the admin key, if there is one, is the admin admission.

steps.title: Build and run
steps.text: build, listen, and serve_until a stop signal.

steps.title: Database
steps.text: A database with the core's tables: in memory in its tests, a SqlitePlace file for its program. The product makes the second swarm in it.

steps.title: Parts
steps.text: The clock and entropy the caller gives (the system's in its program; a fixed clock and seeded entropy in its differential test), and FakeIdentify, which maps made-up bearers to (swarm, role).

steps.title: Config
steps.text: Any bearer is let in, on /mcp, the web page and /mcp-admin alike, for FakeIdentify to judge.

steps.title: Build and run
steps.text: build, then listen on a loopback port and serve until the product is stopped.
